Chapter 7: The Stories We Tell Ourselves
Think about it—everyone has a story running quietly in the background, shaping how they see themselves and the world around them. These stories guide our decisions, color our memories, and influence our actions—often without us even knowing it.
Sometimes, those stories give us confidence, pushing us to take risks and try new things. But other times, they can hold us back, keeping us stuck in the same old habits.
Picture this: there’s a young woman, just starting her first job in a big city. She keeps telling herself she’s not as smart as the people around her—that she’s just lucky to be there. Every little mistake feels like proof she doesn’t belong. Bit by bit, that story she’s telling herself starts to shape her reality. She hesitates, misses out on opportunities, and her self-confidence takes a hit.
But then, something changes. A mentor steps in—someone who sees her strengths and reminds her of all the things she’s already accomplished. With a little encouragement, she starts to rewrite her story. Slowly, she begins to see herself in a new light. And just like that, her world starts to shift.
In another home, there’s a father dealing with unemployment. The story in his head? He’s failed his family. He’ll never find work again. It’s heavy, and it makes everything feel harder—just getting out of bed in the morning becomes a struggle. Then, a friend opens up and shares his own story—his own setbacks and how he got through them. And suddenly, the father realizes he’s not alone. The story changes. It’s not just about failure anymore—it’s about resilience, about facing tough times and finding a way forward.
Meanwhile, a teacher stands in front of a classroom full of restless kids. She’s convinced that some students are just “bad at math.” So, she treats them that way—without even noticing. But one day, she tries something different. She breaks the lessons into smaller steps, celebrates tiny victories, and starts to notice those same kids catching on and even thriving. It hits her: the story she’d believed about who could succeed was wrong. And changing her story changed everything for her students.
These moments really show just how powerful our stories can be. They shape what we notice, what we’re willing to try, and what we believe is possible for ourselves. Most of the time, we don’t even realize those stories are running the show. But here’s the thing—once we become aware of them, we can choose to change them.
Whether it’s the young woman, the father, or the teacher—they all discover that rewriting their stories opens up new possibilities. It’s a reminder that the stories we tell ourselves aren’t just echoes of reality—they actually help create it.
So, what if you started questioning the old narratives you’ve been carrying around? What if you opened yourself up to new possibilities? The truth is, you can start writing a different ending—one that’s truer to who you really are, and where you want to go.
